description:
FILED s440 from agent A's #463 report (pre-existing; reproduces through plain `${$n}`). Repro: `no strict 'refs'; no warnings; my $n = 5; print "1 ", ${$n}, "\n"; print "2 ", $$n, "\n";` -> perl `1 ` / `2 ` (it is $5, undef and read-only), PCL `1 5` / `2 5`. Fix: p-cast-$ resolves a number through %p-symref-box on its string form (same as a string). Bar: the repro; `${"5"}` already? ; a hard ref unchanged; `${\ 5}` (ref to a literal) unchanged; assignment to `${$n}` where $n is a number (perl: modification of a read-only value for $1..$9) vs perl; a Pl/t guard row.

DONE IN PART (s446j, agent J).  SHIPPED: the symbolic-ref READER now reaches the magic scalars.  %p-symref-scalar-value replaces the box-only %p-symref-box lookup at p-cast-$'s string arm, so ${"1"} is $1, ${"10"} is $10 and ${"&"} is $& (the runtime keeps those RAW in their symbol, never in a box, which is why every one of them read undef); a box holding a magic CELL answers through its getter, as the hard-ref arm already did.  WRITE: %p-symref-scalar-set dies perl's "Modification of a read-only value attempted" for the regex-result family (/^[1-9][0-9]*$/ plus & ` ' +), probed: ${"7"} = 1 dies with no match at all, ${"007"} and ${"0"} are ordinary writable variables.  NOT SHIPPED, and this is the finding: the NUMERIC spelling (${$n} with $n == 5) is AMBIGUOUS in the box model and is now task #551 -- %p-hash-unbox-elem hands back the REFERENT box for a scalar ref, so `\42` read out of a container arrives at p-cast-$ as box(42) with is-ref NIL, byte for byte what `my $n = 42` is (measured live).  Treating a number as a symbolic ref made Pl/t/misc-fixes-02.t row 24 (Moo's `local $self->{captures} = {}` idiom) print nothing where perl prints 42 -- a silent wrong in real code traded for a quirk perl programs do not write.  Guard: Pl/t/prefix-incr-deref-01.t (the perl-oracle row + a #551 CANARY row that fails when the residue is fixed).
subject: `${NUMBER}` / `$$n` with a NUMERIC $n is not a symbolic ref: p-cast-$'s `(t inner)` fallback returns the number unchanged (PCL `${$n}` = 5 where perl reads the capture variable $5 -- undef)
